subject: MAP — unit-econ spot audit & pre-close checklist
thread_text:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marco Silva <marco@stratusmed.com>, Priya Balan <priya.b@stratusmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP — unit-econ spot audit & pre-close checklist

Hi Marco / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive MAP session yesterday. As we sync on timing for the pilot close, I wanted to surface a short spot-audit checklist for the token/unit-econ assumptions in the MAP so your finance/engineering teams can validate quickly. This is intended to be a lightweight pass (15–30 mins) to unblock procurement by aligning on the primary levers.

Quick asks:
- Confirm representative traffic profile (tokens per request, requests per minute peak and 95th)
- Validate whether prefix caching is possible for 60% of requests (we used 60% in the workbook)
- Agree on batching target (target latencies vs batch window) — we model a 20ms window at 80ms tail SLA in the workbook
- Call out any regulatory constraints that require private deployment (affects quantization/cost estimates)

I attached an updated MAP workbook (StratusMed_MAP_v2.xlsx) with two scenario tabs: conservative / optimistic. There's also a small sample token_profile_samples.csv illustrating request size distribution we used.

If helpful, Ben or Mina can join a quick 20-min call to walk finance through the cells. Proposed times: Tue 6/29 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 6/30 14:00–14:20 PT.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm which scenario (conservative / optimistic) to baseline for procurement.
2) Finance approves the tokens/$ delta tolerance (we flagged a 12% delta across scenarios).
3) We lock the MAP milestone and schedule the pilot kickoff.

Thanks —
Sean
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marco Silva <marco@stratusmed.com>, Priya Balan <priya.b@stratusmed.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP — unit-econ spot audit & pre-close checklist

Looping in a few clarifications from our ops side —

Marco / Priya — quick notes on the workbook assumptions so finance has context:
- Tokens/unit: the workbook separates prompt tokens and generated tokens. For billing we report total tokens; for caching impact we only reduce generated tokens where prefix can be served from cache.
- Caching feasibility: when you say 60% cacheable, that maps to ~0.6 reduction on generated tokens in those request classes, not on prompt tokens. We can add sensitivity if you prefer a blended reduction.
- Batching: the model in the workbook assumes continuous batching with a max latency cap. If you need deterministic 50ms p95 latency then batching window must be <10ms; that materially reduces token/machine efficiency.
- Quantization/Model variant: Private deployment (on-prem/VPC) may require using int8 or bfloat16 variants which slightly change throughput; we modeled a ~8% cost delta for int8 conversions in the conservative tab.

If you give us 15 mins on Wed we'll highlight where those cells live and which inputs move the biggest cost levers.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer

From: Marco Silva <marco@stratusmed.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Balan <priya@stratusmed.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:23:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MAP — unit-econ spot audit & pre-close checklist

Sean / Ben —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Priya and I reviewed the workbook with our SRE and finance briefly — a few answers and a couple of asks: 

1) Traffic profile: we confirmed a median request size of 420 tokens, 95th at 1,150 tokens. Peak RPS ~ 120 across our busiest region. We uploaded a CSV echoing these numbers.
2) Caching: our clinical triage flows have about ~48% repeatable prompts (patient demographic + fixed triage script) — not 60%. We can scope how much of generated text is fully cacheable; likely closer to 30–35% after including patient-specific slots.
3) Latency SLA: Clinical requires p95 < 150ms; 50–80ms best-effort acceptable. If batching forces p95 > 150ms we cannot accept it for the clinical path — we can batch on a non-critical analytics route.
4) Deployment: we need VPC deployment for PHI controls; we expect quantization is acceptable if it passes inference-quality QA.

Action items for Redwood: please re-run the optimistic/conservative scenarios with 48% cacheable and a batch window that honors p95 < 150ms for clinical flows; show cost delta when batching is disabled for that flow. Also confirm whether Dedicated capacity pricing tier changes unit rate materially versus Hosted (we need both numbers).

We can do Wed 6/30 14:00 PT for the 20-min walkthrough.

—Marco
Director of Engineering, StratusMed

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marco Silva <marco@stratusmed.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP — unit-econ spot audit & pre-close checklist

Thanks Marco — that's exactly the kind of detail we needed. I've attached a quick sensitivity extract to the MAP workbook (saved as StratusMed_MAP_v2.xlsx, tab 'audit_extract') that re-runs both scenarios with 48% cacheable and a split-traffic option where clinical flow is marked "no-batching". Two quick notes from the extract: 

- With clinical excluded from batching, conservative scenario cost per 1M reqs increases by ~18% vs original model; optimistic increases by ~11%.
- Dedicated capacity list-rate reduces per-token compute cost by ~10% versus hosted for the same quantized model (we included a dedicated-rate column). However, committed monthly minimums apply; we flagged a break-even volume in the docs.

I've also exported the token distribution samples we used (token_profile_samples.csv) and left a short comment in the workbook on where to edit prompt/gen split.

Next step: confirm Wed 6/30 14:00 PT for the walkthrough and whether you'd like a short slide (1 page) summarizing delta to share with procurement. If procurement prefers, we can generate a flattened table with worst-case/on-the-record numbers for the PO.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: StratusMed_MAP_v2.xlsx (workbook), token_profile_samples.csv (csv)]
